opening.text: Look closely at an old quilt. Every patch is different. Some are bright. Some are faded. A few are worn thin. Alone, each patch is small. But stitched together, they make a blanket that keeps a whole family warm.
A family is like that quilt. No two members are alike, and no family is perfect. Yet God has placed us together on purpose. Let us look at why that matters.

mainMessage.text: The family is not a side part of God’s plan. It is at the center of it. We belong to each other, and we belong to God. With His help, we can be stitched together in a way that lasts.

blocks.text: **The family is at the center of the quilt.** A good quilt has a pattern, and everything is sewn around it. In the gospel, the family is that center. God’s work is built around parents, children and the bonds between them.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.

President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ” from the October 2025 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The doctrine of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints centers on the family.
The family sits at the heart of the pattern.
**Every patch belongs.** No patch is left out of a quilt. Each of us belongs to a family and to God’s family. We were known and loved before we came to earth. That gives every one of us a place.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ” from the October 2025 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our relationship to God and the purpose of our mortal life are explained in terms of the family.
We are children of God, and that gives us a place.
**Stitched to last.** A quilt can last for generations if the stitching is strong. God offers us a bond that lasts beyond this life. Through the temple, families can be sealed together for eternity.

Foreshadowing the great work to be done in the temples of the Lord in the dispensation of the fulness of times, for the redemption of the dead, and the sealing of the children to their parents, lest the whole earth be smitten with a curse and utterly wasted at his coming.

President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ” from the October 2025 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Essential to our doctrine on the family is the temple.
The temple is how the stitching is made to last.

**Sewn together by shared work.** A quilt comes together when many hands work on it. Families come together the same way. When we do meaningful things together, we learn to love and serve one another.
But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.

President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ” from the October 2025 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Families unite when they do meaningful things together.
Shared work makes strong seams.
**Warm moments hold the seams.** A quilt is meant to warm someone. Happy memories do the same for a family. A meal, a laugh or a quiet prayer together can hold a family close through hard days.

And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.

President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Family-Centered Gospel of Jesus Christ” from the October 2025 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Happy family experiences strengthen family ties.
Joy shared is joy that holds.

**A steady quilt in a cold season.** When the world turns cold, a quilt gives steady warmth. Living by God’s patterns brings stability to a family and to the world around it. Joshua chose that path for his household.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Family Proclamation—Words from God” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Those divine patterns of righteousness lead to stability in our individual lives, our families, and society.
God’s patterns bring steady warmth.

story.title: Joseph Forgives His Brothers

blocks.text: Joseph’s brothers had sold him. Years later, they stood before him in fear. Joseph did not turn them away. He told them God had a purpose, and he embraced them.

Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life. Moreover he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.
A torn family was stitched back together by forgiveness.

story.title: A Father Runs to Welcome His Son

blocks.text: A young man had left home and made many mistakes. When he returned, his father did not wait. He ran to meet him and welcomed him back into the family.

And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
The family is a place where we can come home.

story.title: The Young Warriors and Their Mothers

blocks.text: A group of young men had never fought a battle. Yet they went forward without fear. They had been taught by their mothers to trust God.

Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them. And they rehearsed unto me the words of their mothers, saying: We do not doubt our mothers knew it.
Their courage was wound out of what they learned at home.

story.title: Jesus Provides for His Mother

blocks.text: In His final hours, Jesus was thinking of His family. He saw His mother near the cross. He made sure she would be cared for.

When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.
Even in His suffering, the Savior cared for His family. He shows us what to do.

application.text: First, think of one thing a family member gave you that you want to pass on, such as a story, a value or a tradition. Share it with someone this week.
Second, practice one handoff. Teach someone younger or older something that matters to you.
Third, thank a family member for what they have passed on to you. If you need help in your family, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that families are part of God’s plan for His children. I know that faith and love pass from one generation to the next. I have felt the love of those who came before me. I know that Jesus Christ cares for every family. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of something a family member gave you that you want to pass on.
I invite you to share it with someone this week.
I invite you to thank the person who passed it to you.
blessings: You will carry good things forward.
You will feel a stronger bond across generations.

closingVerse.text: Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.
